discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the establishment of neutrino astronomy with IceCube
motivation: The 2013 IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin opened a new window on the high-energy universe. Later results made it firm: neutrinos coincident with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2018), the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 as a steady source (2022), and the Galactic-plane neutrino emission (2023). Neutrinos are the only messengers that point unambiguously to hadronic accelerators, so these observations directly test cosmic-ray origin models and connect gamma-ray, cosmic-ray and magnetic-field physics into one multi-messenger picture. Francis Halzen conceived the instrumentation of Antarctic ice and led IceCube from AMANDA to its discoveries. Christian Spiering pioneered deep-underwater and under-ice neutrino telescopes through Baikal and AMANDA and shaped the IceCube collaboration. Their work turned a decades-old theoretical idea into a working observational discipline whose measurements now constrain astrophysical models quantitatively.
